---
title: "Phase 2. Design"
description: "Choose the method and plan the assurance your level asks for."
---

You choose the method, finish the assurance level and write the plan.

## What you do

{{< include /guidance/_partials/step-levels-key.qmd >}}

1. [Every level[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} **Choose the method**, and where the work is a model, place it among
   [the eight types of analytical model](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/after-you-have-your-level.qmd#the-eight-types-of-analytical-model).
2. [Every level[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} **Score the likelihood, then read your level.** Follow
   [Step 2, score the likelihood](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/score-the-likelihood.qmd)
   and [Step 3, read your level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/read-your-level.qmd) in the
   Analytical Assurance Decision Tool. Write the finished level into the specification.
   If an impact dimension scored 4, go to [Business Critical analysis](../08-business-critical/index.qmd).
3. [Every level[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} **Write the design and plan**, and share it with everyone involved. Cover:
   - the data, and whether the sources are fit to answer the question
   - the method, and how somebody else running it would get the same results
   - how uncertainty will be identified and communicated
   - the assumptions and known limitations
   - any recommendation in a standard that you do not follow, and why
   - ethics and information governance
   - the outputs, the timescales and the resources
   - the assurance activities

   Where time or resource constrain the approach, tell your commissioner what risks follow.
4. [From Level 2[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} **Turn the level into an assurance plan.** Set out the verification and validation the level
   asks for, and **put time for it in the schedule**. Find what your level asks for in
   [Step 4, what your level requires](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/what-your-level-requires.qmd).
5. [From Level 2[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} **Name your critical friend before the work starts.** They review the plan and confirm they
   can do the assurance it asks for. They put their own time in the schedule.
   - See [find a critical friend](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/what-your-level-requires.qmd#find-a-critical-friend) and
     [how independent they must be at your level](../06-roles/critical-friend.qmd#how-independent-you-have-to-be).
6. [From Level 2[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} **Get the design approved** by your commissioner before work proceeds.

## Outputs of this phase

- The finished assurance level, written into the specification.
- The design and plan, shared with everyone involved.
- [From Level 2[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} The assurance plan, with time in the schedule for it and for your critical friend.
- [From Level 2[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} Your critical friend's name against the work.
- [From Level 2[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} Your commissioner's approval of the design.

## Ready for Phase 3 when

- The assurance level is complete and recorded in the specification.
- The design is approved.
- The assurance plan has time in the schedule, including your critical friend's own time.
- Your critical friend has confirmed they can do the assurance the plan asks for.

## Who does what in this phase

| Role | In Phase 2 |
|---|---|
| **Analyst** | Choose the method. Plan the verification and validation the level asks for. Name your critical friend |
| **Critical friend** | Review the plan. Confirm the assurance planned is at the right level. Put your own time in the schedule |
| **Commissioner** | Approve the design. Make sure there is time and resource for the assurance the level requires |
| **Analysis Senior Responsible Officer** | Business Critical work only. Confirm that organisational governance procedures for design have been followed, before the analysis starts |
